title: Dose-Limiting Toxicity Definitions for Expected Cytopenias in First-in-Human Hematologic Malignancy Trials
summary: How hematologic malignancy FIH protocols define DLTs for expected cytopenias, and what FDA reviews and guidance say about those definitions.
body_markdown:
## Dose-limiting toxicity definitions for expected cytopenias in first-in-human hematologic malignancy trials


### Key points


- Leukemia and MDS protocols in the FDA reviews and registered phase 1 records cited here generally do not count low blood counts, by themselves, as dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). Instead they use a **"prolonged myelosuppression in the absence of leukemia"** construct. A hematologic DLT is a failure of count recovery (usually Grade 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia, often with a hypocellular marrow of <5% cellularity) that persists to a set late timepoint, most often Day 42, with no evidence of residual disease[748](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=748)[684](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=684)[41](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01893320)[44](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=44) .
- The solid-tumor convention (typically Grade 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia, often with a duration criterion, as a DLT in patients without marrow involvement) does not carry over. Pediatric protocols reviewed by FDA show this most clearly: one study used two different hematologic DLT definitions for its solid-tumor and leukemia parts[758](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=758)[684](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=684) .
- FDA reviewers have criticized cytopenia DLT definitions that are too permissive. In the Vyxeos (CPX-351) review, the reviewer called the timing and degree of cytopenia in the DLT definition "quite liberal." The reviewer said that leniency could account for toxicity seen in later studies, which ended in reduced induction and consolidation schedules[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=606) .
- FDA guidance does not set numeric hematologic DLT thresholds for hematologic malignancies. Its expectations are procedural. CBER's CAR T guidance says DLTs should be well defined. Any exemptions should be justified. Observation periods should capture both acute and delayed toxicity. The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) should not be treated by default as the dose to carry forward[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=518)[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=523)[298](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=298) .
- FDA does not publish clinical hold letters. Sponsor disclosures describe holds in hematologic malignancy programs that later led to changes in DLT definitions or dose finding, though none was tied to expected cytopenias. Examples include adding severe cytokine release syndrome as a DLT and requiring more patients at lower doses before enrollment resumed[128](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1594864/000119312515182467/d882196d10q.htm)[553](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000110820523000023/cris-20221231.htm) .


### Why the standard hematologic DLT fails in leukemia and MDS


In patients with active myeloid disease, cytopenias are usually present at enrollment and are part of the disease. In the revumenib review, FDA noted that a large share of participants had high-grade cytopenias at baseline: Grade 3 to 4 neutrophils in 80%, platelets in 77% and hemoglobin in 41%. That left "too few participants with high enough cell counts for credible shift analyses"[427](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=427)[428](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=428) . EMA's anticancer guideline makes the same point. Myelosuppression, infections and bleeding can be symptoms of the underlying hematologic malignancy, which makes attribution difficult in single-arm studies[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=174) . EMA's appendix on hematologic malignancies adds that bone marrow failure is often present at diagnosis and worsened by treatment, so dose reduction for this reason is often not indicated, unlike in solid tumors[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=175) .


Protocols handle this in two ways:


- **Excluding blood counts from MTD determination entirely** , with a narrow exception. A pediatric decitabine-cytarabine leukemia protocol states that "low blood counts per se are not considered to be dose-limiting toxicities." Hematologic toxicity is assessed only in responding patients who have Grade 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia due to a hypoplastic marrow at Day 42 in the absence of leukemia[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=62) .
- **Assuming baseline cytopenias are disease-related** and defining DLT only as treatment-attributable marrow aplasia. A CPX-351 plus palbociclib protocol states that "low counts at diagnosis are due to involvement by the disease process and require therapy for improvement." It then defines hematologic DLT as severe myelosuppression with a hypoplastic marrow (<5% cellularity) and no evidence of leukemia 45 days from start of therapy[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=60)[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=59) .


The pediatric ruxolitinib study ADVL1011 shows the split directly. Its DLT observation period was the first 28 days of cycle 1[755](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=755) . In Part A (solid tumors), only patients without marrow involvement and with adequate baseline counts could be evaluated for hematologic toxicity. Grade 4 thrombocytopenia or Grade 4 neutropenia was a DLT[758](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=758) . In Part B (leukemias and MPNs), the hematologic DLT was "failure to recover a peripheral ANC > 500/mm³ and platelets > 20,000/mm³ by 42 days after the first treatment day, not due to malignant infiltration"[684](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=684) . An FDA review of a pediatric vinorelbine phase 1 study (CCG-0936) likewise shows a solid-tumor-style definition (Grade 4 toxicity lasting ≥7 days in patients without marrow involvement). Patients with leukemia, lymphoma or marrow involvement were excluded from hematologic DLT evaluability under that definition[695](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=695)[696](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=696) .


### The "prolonged myelosuppression in the absence of leukemia" construct


Across FDA reviews and ClinicalTrials.gov protocol records, the hematologic DLT for myeloid malignancies usually combines four elements:


1. **A count threshold** : typically ANC <500/µL and/or platelets below 10,000 to 25,000/µL, or Grade ≥4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia.
2. **Marrow evidence of treatment effect rather than disease** : hypocellularity (most often <5%), and in some protocols blasts <5%.
3. **A late assessment timepoint** : most often Day 42 from the start of cycle 1, though protocols range from 28 to 56 days.
4. **An explicit attribution exclusion** : no evidence of active leukemia, MDS or malignant infiltration.


#### Examples from FDA reviews


Product (review) Hematologic DLT language Timepoint


Tibsovo (ivosidenib), NDA 211192 "Prolonged myelosuppression with the persistence of grade ≥ 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia in the absence of leukemia (blast count < 5%) at least 42 days after the initiation of Cycle 1 therapy"; DLTs evaluated during Cycle 1[748](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=748) ≥42 days


Daurismo (glasdegib), phase 1B ANC <500/µL or platelets <10 x 10^9/L lasting longer than 42 days from detection, "with a normal BM (<5% blasts and no evidence of disease or dysplasia)"[692](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=692) >42 days from detection


Jakafi (ruxolitinib), pediatric ADVL1011 Part B Failure to recover ANC >500/mm³ and platelets >20,000/mm³ by Day 42, "not due to malignant infiltration"[684](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=684) Day 42


Vyxeos (CPX-351) dose escalation "no evidence of AML, persistent BM cellularity of <20%, and peripheral ANC of <500/mcl and/or platelet count <10,000/mcl, or persistent platelet transfusion dependence"; observation period was the first cycle[745](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=745)[744](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=744) First cycle (no numeric day threshold stated)


Gleevec (imatinib), clinical review "For patients with leukemia, DLT will be defined as a duration of bone marrow aplasia > 5 weeks from the first treatment day"[682](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=682) >5 weeks


The Vyxeos review also lists "persistent cytopenias beyond 56 days" among dose-limiting adverse events. One of the three DLTs observed at 134 units/m² was persistent hypocellularity beyond Study Day 56[645](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=645)[650](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=650) .


#### Examples from registered phase 1 protocols


Trial Hematologic DLT language


NCT04079296 (ASP7517) ANC <500/µL "for more than 28 days off therapy and in the absence of evidence of active leukemia or MDS"; also new Grade 4 thrombocytopenia with ≥2-grade worsening from baseline within 24 hours of dosing[38](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04079296)


NCT01893320 (vosaroxin + decitabine); NCT01891981 (moxetumomab) Severe myelosuppression with a hypoplastic marrow (<5% cellularity) and no evidence of leukemia 42 days from start of therapy[41](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01893320)[50](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01891981)


NCT02418000 (E6201) NCI leukemia-specific criteria: marrow cellularity <5% at ≥6 weeks without evidence of leukemia[40](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02418000)


NCT05168202 (CC-95251) Grade 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia persisting at Day 28 without active AML/MDS; prolonged myelosuppression >42 days without active leukemia; Cycle 1 window Days 1 to 28, extendable to 42[42](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05168202)


NCT02848001 (CC-90009) Marrow cellularity <5% **or** persistent Grade >3 neutropenia at Cycle 1 Day 42 in the absence of leukemia[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=51)


NCT03701295 (pinometostat + azacitidine) Grade 4 neutropenia lasting >42 days in absence of active leukemia; patients with Day 28 cytopenias are followed to Day 42 before escalation, and recovery between Days 28 and 42 means no hematologic DLT[44](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=44)[45](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=45)


NCT02416908 (CLAG + selinexor) Marrow cellularity <5% on Day 42 or later without leukemia; persistent Grade ≥3 neutropenia >42 days without leukemia[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=53)[54](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=54)


Note that the 42-day assessment often runs past a 28-day DLT window. Protocols handle this by extending observation for patients with unresolved cytopenias before the next dose-level decision[45](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=45) , or by letting late myelosuppression DLTs update dose assignment after the 28-day evaluable period[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=58) .


#### Common exemptions


Febrile neutropenia is often carved out. ASP7517 excluded "Grade 3 febrile neutropenia with or without infection"[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=39) . CLAG plus selinexor excluded Grade 4 neutropenia lasting >7 days, febrile neutropenia, Grade ≥3 thrombocytopenia with or without bleeding, and infection-related complications[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=55) . The Vyxeos definition also excepted Grade 3 febrile neutropenia among non-hematologic toxicities[746](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=746) . As discussed below, FDA's view of a permissive package like the Vyxeos definition is not necessarily favorable.


### Lymphoid malignancies, myeloma and T-cell engagers


In lymphoma, CLL and myeloma, baseline marrow failure is less universal. FDA reviews of recent programs mostly describe the DLT window rather than cytopenia-specific carve-outs:


- In MajesTEC-1 (teclistamab), the weekly-dosing DLT period was changed to 21 days to cover three doses, or 28 days if step-up dosing was used[617](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=617) . A later amendment clarified that "Grade 4 hematologic toxicity does not require discontinuation in Phase 1 unless the event also meets DLT criteria"[464](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=464) . FDA agreed with the applicant's summary of protocol amendments[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=465) .
- Linvoseltamab (R5458-ONC-1826) used a modified 3+3 (4+3) design with a 28-day DLT observation period. FDA agreed with the study design description[607](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=607)[608](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=608) .
- Elranatamab study C1071009 designated Cycle 2 as the DLT period in its dose-determination parts[610](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=610) . Zanubrutinib (BGB-3111-AU-003) used Weeks 1 to 3[612](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=612) . Acalabrutinib (ACE-CL-001) used a 28-day DLT period[619](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=619) .


For CAR T cells, CBER's guidance gives example DLTs centered on CRS, neurotoxicity, autoimmune, allergic and organ toxicity[519](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=519)[520](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=520)[521](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=521)[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=522) . CBER's CAR T guidance examples do not list prolonged cytopenias as DLTs or as exemptions. Still, FDA has treated post-CAR T marrow toxicity as a serious risk. In the Abecma review, severe prolonged cytopenia requiring stem cell rescue in three subjects led FDA to conclude that marrow toxicity "may be more severe than observed with CD 19 CAR T therapy." FDA modified the boxed warning to include prolonged cytopenia[259](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=259)[260](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=260) .


### What FDA has said about DLT definitions


#### FDA guidance: procedural expectations, not numeric thresholds


- **CAR T guidance.** "We recommend DLTs be well defined in the clinical protocol." The guidance says the definition may vary with the underlying disease, and "any exception or exemption of treatment-emergent toxicities from the DLT definition should be clearly described and justified." It adds that "the observation period for DLTs should be adequate to capture both acute and delayed toxicities"[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=518)[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=523) . DLTs should be defined "independent of attribution to CAR T cells unless a clear alternative cause can be described"[524](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=524) . Example stopping rules include more than two Grade 4 CRS events for a first-in-human CAR T product, or any death within 30 days of administration[526](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=526) . The attribution principle bears directly on blanket disease-related cytopenia exemptions: sponsors should be ready to justify why an exclusion is warranted.
- **Oncology dosage optimization guidance.** The historical MTD approach comes from cytotoxic chemotherapy[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=289) . Targeted therapies may have similar activity below the MTD, or an MTD may never be reached[295](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=295) . Selecting the MTD or maximum administered dose can produce "an unnecessarily high" labeled dosage that harms tolerability and patients' ability to remain on treatment[298](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=298) .
- **Expansion cohorts guidance (March 2022).** When the therapeutic index is narrow and dose-escalation DLTs may be fatal or cause serious morbidity, FDA strongly recommends delaying expansion until sufficient data establish the recommended phase 2 dose[198](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=198) .
- **Therapeutic cancer vaccines guidance.** Protocols should clearly define DLTs, off-treatment criteria and study stopping rules, whatever escalation approach is used[201](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=201) .
- **Radiopharmaceutical dosage draft guidance.** A one-cycle DLT period may suffice for initial escalation. When multiple cycles are intended, cumulative toxicity should be assessed using data from multiple cycles and dose levels[320](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=320)[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=301) .
- **ICH S9 (adopted by FDA).** Phase 1 trials in advanced cancer may dose to MTD and DLT[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=290) . Where nonclinical data show a steep dose-response for severe toxicity or no preceding marker, S9 calls for smaller-than-usual (fractional) escalation increments[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=9) .


The FDA guidances cited here do not set baseline-adjusted count thresholds, recovery durations or marrow criteria for hematologic DLTs in hematologic malignancies. The draft MDS guidance notes that anemia and neutropenia are expected with many MDS drugs, but it does not supply DLT criteria[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=203) . By contrast, EMA's anticancer guideline (Revision 6) says MTD and DLT must be carefully predefined "to capture relevant toxicities and arrive at a useful RP2D." For targeted and immunomodulating agents, it says broader definitions and longer observation periods may be appropriate[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=172) .


#### FDA review commentary


- **Vyxeos (CPX-351): cytopenia DLT definition too permissive.** The reviewer wrote: "the timing and degree of cytopenia included in this DLT definition are quite liberal and could account for the toxicity seen in subsequent studies that ultimately led to a decreased schedule in induction 2 (2 vs 3 doses), and a decreased dose and schedule in consolidation (65 units/m^2 x 2 doses rather than 100 units/m^2 x 3 doses)"[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=606) . The definition required persistent marrow cellularity <20% plus severe cytopenias or transfusion dependence over the first cycle, without AML[745](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=745) . The reviewer also noted a positive correlation between dose and toxicity in the dose-finding study, "as is expected with a cytotoxic agent"[652](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=652) .
- **Pediatric vinorelbine (CCG-0936): excluding patients from DLT assessment.** The FDA reviewer accepted analyses by marrow involvement as sensitivity analyses. The reviewer noted, however, that all phase 1 patients usually contribute to DLT/MTD assessment and many had been excluded[697](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=697) . The reviewer also observed that the defined MTD of 33.75 mg/m² "was too toxic in the Phase II study," and the dose was lowered to 30 mg/m² weekly[698](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=698) . This is a solid-tumor-focused protocol, but the comment shows FDA's concern with evaluability carve-outs.
- **Mylotarg (gemtuzumab ozogamicin).** A reviewer commented on a study with "limitations with regards to retrospective determination of DLTs"[723](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=723) .
- **Epcoritamab (GCT3013-04): DLT criteria revised on regulatory feedback.** Amendment 1 (July 1, 2020) stated that "based on regulatory authority feedback," the protocol was amended to clarify DLT criteria. It added "any AE considered related to epcoritamab treatment that causes a delay in dosing of >7 days"[623](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=623) . FDA agreed with the amendment summary[751](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=751) . The review does not identify which authority gave the feedback.
- **Revumenib (SNDX-5613-0700): DLT definition as a Type C topic.** FDA held a Type C meeting on December 15, 2020 "regarding QTc criteria in the DLT definition"[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=358) . Protocol version 7.0 had raised the QTc DLT threshold from any Grade 2 to any Grade 3[356](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=356)[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=357) . On hematopoiesis, the clinical team lead concluded the data "are clearly not adequate to assess for an impact of revumenib on hematopoiesis." The data were "not sufficient to conclude that anemia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia are ARs"[432](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=432) .
- **MTD not used as the dose.** For ivosidenib, an MTD was not established. The 500 mg dose was selected based on PK/PD, safety and efficacy, and the observed DLTs were QTc prolongation and rash[396](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=396)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=391) . For glasdegib, the MTD in hematologic malignancies was 400 mg, but the recommended dose was 100 mg[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=459)[460](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=460) . For olutasidenib, no DLTs were observed, the MTD was not determined, and FDA agreed with 150 mg BID based on efficacy, safety, PK and PD[474](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=474)[473](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=473) .
- **Imetelstat (Rytelo): gaps in hematologic data.** FDA noted that essentially one dose level was evaluated in the lower-risk MDS population[381](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=381) . It also noted that hematology labs "were not consistently collected in the early phase studies," which hindered dose-response analysis[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=384) .
- **Inqovi.** FDA agreed with the applicant's proposed dose modification strategy for hematological toxicity, including the dose-reduction schema[502](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=502) .


### Clinical holds in hematologic malignancy programs


FDA hold letters are not public, so the record comes from sponsor SEC disclosures. In the sponsor disclosures cited here, no hold was attributed specifically to expected cytopenias or myelosuppression. Several holds in hematologic malignancy programs nonetheless led to changes in DLT definitions, dose levels or safety monitoring:


- **Juno JCAR015 (relapsed/refractory ALL).** In early 2014, the hold followed two deaths believed related to severe CRS[127](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1594864/000119312515182467/d882196d10q.htm) . The changes that led to removal included lower dosing, eligibility exclusions, **adding severe CRS as a DLT** , and prohibiting retreatment after prior nonhematologic Grade 4 toxicity[128](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1594864/000119312515182467/d882196d10q.htm) .
- **Curis emavusertib (TakeAim Leukemia and Lymphoma), April 2022.** FDA placed partial holds and asked for data on a deceased AML patient who had rhabdomyolysis, an identified DLT. It also asked for safety and efficacy data, the recommended phase 2 dose determination, and proposed protocol changes[123](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000110820522000005/cris-20220331.htm) . The lymphoma hold was lifted in August 2022. Lifting required a rhabdomyolysis identification and management strategy, at least nine more patients at 200 mg, and at least six more at 100 mg with ibrutinib[552](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000110820523000023/cris-20221231.htm)[553](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000110820523000023/cris-20221231.htm) . For leukemia, Phase 1a monotherapy dose finding resumed with at least nine more patients at 200 mg. Phase 2a expansion and combinations with azacitidine or venetoclax stayed on hold pending completion of Phase 1a[554](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000110820522000023/cris-20220930.htm)[555](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000110820523000023/cris-20221231.htm) .
- **Kura ziftomenib (KOMET-001), November 2021.** A partial hold followed a Grade 5 event potentially associated with differentiation syndrome. It was lifted on January 20, 2022 after agreement on a differentiation syndrome mitigation strategy[550](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1422143/000095017022001967/kura-20211231.htm)[551](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1422143/000095017022001967/kura-20211231.htm) .
- **Foghorn FHD-286 (AML/MDS), August 2022.** A full hold followed suspected fatal differentiation syndrome. It was lifted June 1, 2023[119](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1822462/000162828023020737/fhtx_amlxpressxreleasexjun.htm) , with an amended protocol and planned combinations with decitabine or low-dose cytarabine[120](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1822462/000162828023020737/fhtx_amlxpressxreleasexjun.htm) .
- **Curis CUDC-427 (solid tumors or lymphoma).** After a partial hold, the amended protocol used 14 days on / 7 days off in 21-day cycles with standard 3+3 escalation[126](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108205/000119312515060006/d846591d10k.htm) .


Separately, Geron amended its imetelstat myelofibrosis pilot study to raise hematologic thresholds for retreatment and add stricter monitoring and dose-adjustment criteria for severe, persistent cytopenias. The disclosure does not link this amendment to an FDA hold[242](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886744/000104746915001989/a2223360z10-k.htm) .


### Practical implications for protocol drafting


Based on these sources, a first-in-human hematologic DLT definition in a hematologic malignancy is more likely to hold up in review if it:


- Defines hematologic DLT as a failure of count recovery with marrow evidence of treatment-related hypoplasia and no residual disease, at a stated timepoint (Day 42 is the most common convention)[748](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=748)[41](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01893320) .
- States how the DLT window and the hematologic assessment timepoint fit together, including what happens to dose-escalation decisions while Day 28 to 42 recovery is pending[45](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=45)[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=58) .
- Justifies each exemption, especially for febrile neutropenia, infections and bleeding, in line with FDA's CAR T guidance on describing and justifying exceptions[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=523) . As Vyxeos shows, permissive cytopenia criteria can lead to dose and schedule reductions later[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=606) .
- Avoids excluding large subsets of patients from DLT evaluability without a clear rationale[697](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=697) .
- Gathers hematology data consistently across dose levels and over time, so exposure-response for cytopenias can be assessed later[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=384) . It should not rely on the MTD alone for dose selection[298](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/dose-limiting-toxicity-definitions-for-expected?showSourceNumber=298) .
